projects.title: BURRA POD
projects.subtitle: Community centre · Fleet Street, North Parramatta, NSW
projects.statement:
Burra Pod is a community centre shaped by movement, adaptation and connection to place. Inspired by Indigenous understandings that the best journeys in life are almost never linear or straightforward, this design incorporates flowing pathways which invite exploration and encounter. Located on Durug Country in North Parramatta, the building concept takes inspiration from the fluid movements of eels and their enduring relationship with the river, translating these qualities into organic forms and a continuous spatial flow through the spaces of the building.

Water is carried through the project as both a spatial and sensory element, reinforcing ideas of movement, inspiring learning and connection to Country. A water feature within the building and public space strengthens the relationship, creating moments of immersive experiences, reflection and curiosity.

The program supports gathering, learning in a central courtyard that forms the heart of the project. The spatial journey reflects a process of becoming, guiding individuals from identity, discovery and application, towards exploration and contribution. Spaces for making, storytelling, exhibition and intergenerational exchange allow personal experience and knowledge to develop into collective understanding. Native planting, water and interpretive landscape elements strengthen engagement with Country, encouraging visitors to learn from the ecological and cultural history of the area.

projects.title: AXIS CITY CENTRE
projects.subtitle: Waterloo Estate Redevelopment
projects.statement:
Aligning movement, people & space.

Axis Waterloo City Centre is designed as an inclusive civic hub that prioritises accessibility, connection and belonging. Organised around a central axis, the project creates a clear movement spine that links public spaces, built areas and landscape zones into one coherent experience.

A key aim is accessibility for all. The design supports people of different ages, abilities and needs through open circulation, clear pathways and spaces that are easy to navigate. The centre also integrates with the natural topography of the site, using stepped platforms, terraces and layered levels to create a building that responds to the land rather than flattening it.

Each space is designed to offer a distinct and interesting experience. The open communal areas encourage gathering and interaction, while quieter zones provide places for rest and reflection. Terraces create elevated views across the site, shaded walkways make movement comfortable, and landscaped pockets soften the built form. Dedicated spaces for families, workers, students, visitors and community groups ensure the centre remains flexible and inclusive.

Overall, Axis Waterloo City Centre aims to become a vibrant, human-centred place where people can meet, move, relax, work, learn and stay.

projects.title: OASIS
projects.statement:
Aligning movement, people & space.

This project is derived from the radical model "Held in the Hands of Time", which explores how water and time shape form. Water flow acts as both a metaphor and a spatial organiser, guiding visitors through a hydrological experience of pooling, meandering and releasing: a circulation that unfolds as a slow journey, engaging with the Coal Loader's industrial past through eroded forms and carved voids, showing how architecture is also shaped by time.

projects.title: WEAVE
projects.subtitle: Facade Design
projects.statement:
A north-facing facade design for a couple living in a small double-storey house near the Northern Beaches, directly opposite a public park. Active and health conscious, they love walks in nature, waking up to natural light, growing their own food and filling their home with plants.

  • North-facing facade with high sun exposure, the driest face of the building
  • Opposite a public park, balancing privacy with interaction with nature
  • Flat roof for planting
  • Skylight void to emphasise the permeability and openness of the facade structure
  • Half-level bedroom with a balcony, connecting both levels and the views
